Alger, 15 novembre 2026 (Algeria Tech) —: Algiers, November 15, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — The National Portal for Government Digital Services, Dzair Digital Services, has recorded nearly two million registered users, four months after its official launch on July 5, 2026. The platform currently brings together seventy-one digital services intended for Algerian citizens.
Bilan des démarches dématérialisées et c: Assessment of digital procedures and regulatory framework
S'exprimant lors de l'émission « L’invit: Speaking on the "L’invité du jour" program on Channel 3 of Algerian Radio, Hacene Derrar, an expert with the High Commission for Digitization (HCN), presented data regarding the usage of the Dzair Digital Services platform. In addition to the registered users, the portal recorded eleven million visits and enabled the issuance of over nine hundred thousand digital documents. According to the HCN representative, these volumes demonstrate the population's interest in digital administrative procedures, which help reduce costs and simplify access to public services.
L'expert a insisté sur la valeur juridiq: The expert emphasized the legal value of documents issued online, stating that they have strict equivalence with standard paper formats and that no administrative structure has the right to reject them. In response to rejections observed in the field, the High Commission for Digitization provides a complaint interface on its own portal. This space allows users to report any incident, attach the contested document, and track the processing of their file. This provision is based on instructions from the Prime Minister urging all sectors to accept these original supports, while a specific mechanism has been developed by HCN to verify the authenticity of files.
Pour favoriser l'appropriation du systèm: To encourage the adoption of the system by public agents, HCN conducted a training session on November 2 to introduce administrative executives to the use of the verification and authentication tool. An information day addressing the adoption of digital documents was also held on November 10, bringing together representatives from almost all administrative sectors.
